Method of Attack: Cryptocurrency clipboard hijacking to replace victim's wallet address with attacker's
Persistence via registry key or scheduled task to run malware at startup or every minute
Disguised as fake hacking tools distributed mainly via Telegram and blog
Malware packed in ZIP with executable launching fake UI to trick victims
Impacted Systems: Windows systems (implied by registry key and scheduled task usage)
Indicators of Compromise: Telegram Hack Boss channel with ~2,800 subscribers and ~9 posts/month
Over 100 cryptocurrency wallet addresses (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, Monero, Dogecoin) associated with HackBoss
GitHub page by Avast with hashes and names of fake applications disguising HackBoss malware
Date of Discovery: Reported by Avast in blog post dated around 2023 (exact date not specified)
